Calculate reflection and transmission using a defined excitation and reference.
Choose the port model before comparing S-parameters between geometries or solvers.

## Geometric ports, simulation locators, and terminals

| Object | Meaning | What the reader selects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GDSFactory connection port | Position, orientation, width, layer, and type at a component connection plane. It lets layout instances connect. | A matching cross-section and actual child port. |
| OrcaPen simulation locator | A named port identifying component-owned sheet or marker geometry. Its `sim_*` type describes a locator role. | The qualified locator name and intended source geometry. |
| Solver port or terminal | An electrical assignment to conductors and supporting geometry for the chosen problem. | Signal/reference conductors, ordering, direction, excitation, and normalization. |

A connection port does not automatically become an excitation. A simulation
locator does not add its own metal, sheet polygon, mesh size, impedance, or
circuit element. The component authors geometry; the SCGSim problem assigns its
electrical meaning. For ordinary placement and connection, follow
[GDSFactory instances and ports](https://gdsfactory.github.io/gdsfactory/notebooks/01_references/).

### OrcaPen locator helpers

The public [port helpers](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/c4dbf7a88166f5817ffbac5fc4182a7a429ae69b/orcapen_sc_pdk/port_operations.py)
add a named GDSFactory port to existing component geometry. Each takes the
component plus `name`, `center`, `layer`, and optional `width` and `orientation`.
Physical centres and widths use µm; read returned ports through `dcenter` and
`dwidth`.

| Helper | Registered locator type | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add_mesh_port()` | `sim_mesh` | Identify a feature for local mesh selection; choose mesh lengths in the simulation. |
| `add_junction_lumped_port()` | `sim_junction_lumped` | Identify a junction sheet; choose linearized inductance and other problem controls separately. |
| `add_driven_lumped_port()` | `sim_lumped` | Identify an excitation sheet; choose resistance, source, and activity in the solver problem. |

The [type registry](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/c4dbf7a88166f5817ffbac5fc4182a7a429ae69b/orcapen_sc_pdk/port_metadata.py)
also declares `sim_cpw`, `sim_terminal`, `sim_wave`, and `sim_current`.
PDK activation registers these strings with GDSFactory; a type label alone is
not a Palace or AEDT assignment.

For example, [SimplePad](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/c4dbf7a88166f5817ffbac5fc4182a7a429ae69b/orcapen_sc_pdk/cells/simulation/scgsim/simple_pad.py)
draws a nonmetal east-gap sheet on `D0_TOP_SIM_BOUNDARY` and locates it with
`o_junction_lumped`. The optional inductance belongs to the eigenmode problem,
not the locator. In a component hierarchy, select its actual qualified name
(for example `chip/o_junction_lumped`) together with its intended conductor pair.

For Q2D, author native section conductors and their reference grouping in the
[Cross-section Simulation](q2d-cross-section.qmd) tutorial; geometric connection
ports are not that model's voltage-source definitions.

## Terminal excitation

The CPW–meander examples keep the resonator and airbridges while changing
the excitation geometry.

| Port kind | Geometry and reference | Tutorial |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lumped | Internal nonmetal Signal–Ground support sheets and launchers | [HFSS Lumped Terminal](../../notebooks/SCGSimExamples/ComponentSimulation/CpwMeanderAirbridge/aedt_hfss_driven_terminal_lumped.ipynb) · <a href="../../notebooks/SCGSimExamples/ComponentSimulation/CpwMeanderAirbridge/aedt_hfss_driven_terminal_lumped.ipynb" data-noresolveinput download>IPYNB</a> · <a href="../../notebooks/src/SCGSimExamples/ComponentSimulation/CpwMeanderAirbridge/aedt_hfss_driven_terminal_lumped.qmd" data-noresolveinput download>QMD</a> |
| Wave | Constant-width CPW ends at exterior cuts | [HFSS Wave Terminal](../../notebooks/SCGSimExamples/ComponentSimulation/CpwMeanderAirbridge/aedt_hfss_driven_terminal_wave.ipynb) · <a href="../../notebooks/SCGSimExamples/ComponentSimulation/CpwMeanderAirbridge/aedt_hfss_driven_terminal_wave.ipynb" data-noresolveinput download>IPYNB</a> · <a href="../../notebooks/src/SCGSimExamples/ComponentSimulation/CpwMeanderAirbridge/aedt_hfss_driven_terminal_wave.qmd" data-noresolveinput download>QMD</a> |

Use the tutorial's AEDT/SCGSim environment. Preserve the source/reference
conductors, ordered ports, integration directions, normalization,
de-embedding, and renormalization choices.
The [Model Gallery](../../public-pdk-examples/test-components.md#driven-terminal-lumped-and-wave-port-comparison)
shows the two source layouts.

For a TSV-stitched line, see the separate
[TSV Terminal workflow](../tsv-model-inspection.qmd).

## Modal port models {#modal-port-models}

Terminal and Modal are different solution interpretations; Wave is a port kind.
The [finite-CPW Driven Modal note](../../notebooks/SCGSimExamples/ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround/aedt_hfss_driven_modal.ipynb) · <a href="../../notebooks/SCGSimExamples/ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround/aedt_hfss_driven_modal.ipynb" data-noresolveinput download>IPYNB</a> · <a href="../../notebooks/src/SCGSimExamples/ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround/aedt_hfss_driven_modal.qmd" data-noresolveinput download>QMD</a>
describes its intended model.

⏳ That Modal note is not a runnable solver tutorial. Use the Terminal examples
above for the available full workflow; keep their conductor-reference convention.

## Read the response

Inspect native port assignments before solving. Read returned S-data with
frequency samples, port ordering, reference impedance, and adaptive history.
Keep setup adaptation separate from sweep completion.

Touchstone reference impedance and a solved Wave-port characteristic impedance
are different quantities. For the layout recipes and reported geometric ports,
see [Cross-sections](../../public-pdk-examples/cross-sections.qmd).
